questions.q: Put the expense lifecycle stages in order: Submit, Incur, Account, Audit and Approve, Capture, Reimburse.
options: Incur, Capture, Submit, Audit and Approve, Account, Reimburse
Submit, Incur, Capture, Reimburse, Account, Audit and Approve
Account, Incur, Submit, Capture, Audit and Approve, Reimburse
Reimburse, Incur, Capture, Submit, Account, Audit and Approve
questions.explain: The correct order is: incur, capture, submit, audit and approve, account, reimburse.

questions.q: When is a true hard limit (one that blocks submission entirely) typically used?
options: For every single expense type without exception
Only for airfare
Only for a small number of expense types where leadership decided no justification should be possible
Hard limits do not exist in Oracle Fusion Expenses
questions.explain: Hard limits are reserved for cases like a strict company-wide prohibition, such as no personal mileage reimbursement on a company car.

questions.q: At what level is almost every Expenses setup object (templates, policies, audit rules) defined?
options: Once globally for the entire company
Per business unit
Per individual employee
Per invoice
questions.explain: Expenses setup objects are scoped per business unit so different parts of a company can have different rules, currencies, and policies.

questions.q: In the worked example, what was the first step before adding 'Parking' as a new expense type for Field Services?
options: Immediately rewriting the Hotel policy limit
Checking whether Parking already exists as a seeded expense type under Ground Transportation
Deleting the Field Services business unit
Creating an entirely new chart of accounts
questions.explain: Because Parking is typically a seeded expense type already, the first step is checking whether it needs to be activated rather than created from scratch.

questions.q: What are the two layers of every expense report in Oracle Fusion Expenses?
options: The report header and the expense items
The approval queue and the payment file
The chart of accounts and the ledger
The corporate card and the bank statement
questions.explain: A report consists of a header (purpose, template, business unit) and one or more expense items, each with its own type, date, and amount.

questions.q: How does Castellan actually pay an approved cash advance to the employee?
options: Through Oracle Fusion Payables, as a standalone payment
By mailing physical cash
It is automatically deducted from the General Ledger with no payment
Advances are never actually paid, only promised
questions.explain: Once approved, the advance is paid through Payables using the same payment infrastructure used for expense reimbursements.

questions.q: What happens to a corporate card transaction the moment it arrives from the card issuer's feed?
options: It immediately posts to the General Ledger
It immediately reimburses the employee
It lands as an unassigned card transaction that the employee must review and attach to a report
It is automatically deleted after 24 hours
questions.explain: Transactions arrive as unassigned items in a queue; nothing posts to the ledger or gets reimbursed until the employee attaches it to a submitted expense report.

questions.q: Why does Castellan use per diem for domestic travel but itemized meal receipts for international trips?
options: Per diem is simpler to audit domestically, while actual meal costs vary too widely internationally for one schedule to be fair
International employees are not allowed to claim any meals
Per diem is illegal outside the United States
There is no reason; the choice is arbitrary
questions.explain: A company chooses per diem or itemized meals deliberately per business unit or trip type based on how well a fixed rate reflects real costs.

questions.q: What is the difference between a report-level and an employee-level audit trigger?
options: There is no difference; both terms mean the same thing
An employee-level trigger only applies to managers
A report-level trigger evaluates the current report alone; an employee-level trigger looks backward across an employee's history
A report-level trigger can never be automated
questions.explain: Report-level rules catch one-off issues on a single report; employee-level rules catch patterns, like repeated missing-receipt declarations, across multiple reports over time.

questions.q: Why does Oracle route expense reimbursement through the standard Payables invoice process rather than a separate payment mechanism?
options: So that reimbursements automatically inherit existing Payables controls like payment terms, holds, and AP aging reporting
Because Payables invoices are always paid instantly with no review
Because expense reports cannot otherwise be tracked at all
Because it is required by law in every country
questions.explain: Reusing the invoice process means reimbursements get all the existing payment controls and reporting without building a second pipeline.

questions.q: In the duplicate-hotel-item example, how was the accidental overpayment recovered?
options: It was written off with no further action
By deducting the duplicate amount from the employee's next approved expense report, with a documented note
By firing the employee
By reversing the employee's salary for the month
questions.explain: The overpayment was recovered as a deduction against the employee's next approved report, tracked clearly rather than silently erased.

questions.q: Can more than one approval rule set apply to the same expense report at the same time?
options: No, only one rule set can ever be active company-wide
Only if the report has zero expense items
Only on reports under $10
Yes, multiple rule sets can run in parallel, such as supervisor approval plus cost center owner approval
questions.explain: Castellan's own setup combines ExpenseReportRuleSet and CostCenterRuleSet in parallel for reports that cross cost centers.

questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion Expenses generate accounting events for Subledger Accounting to interpret, rather than posting directly to the General Ledger?
options: Because direct posting is technically impossible in any Oracle module
Because Subledger Accounting is unrelated to Expenses
Because the General Ledger cannot accept expense transactions
To get the same audit trail, preview-before-posting capability, and consistent multi-currency/intercompany handling used by Payables and Receivables
questions.explain: Using Subledger Accounting gives Expenses the same architecture benefits already seen in Payables and Receivables, rather than needing separate custom logic.

questions.q: In Ticket 1, why did Jordan Reyes's mileage claim calculate a lower amount than expected?
options: The updated $0.67/mile rate schedule had an effective date that started too late
He drove fewer miles than he claimed
His manager rejected the claim
Mileage claims require a receipt that he didn't attach
questions.explain: The new rate schedule's effective date was entered a week too late, so his claim processed under the old $0.65 rate instead.

questions.q: What does Process Expense Reimbursement create in step 4 of the trail?
options: A standard Payables invoice referencing the originating expense report
A new expense policy
A corporate card feed mapping
A journal entry directly in the GL with no invoice
questions.explain: Process Expense Reimbursement generates a standard Payables invoice, carrying a reference back to the original expense report.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a question OTBI can answer that a fixed seeded report likely cannot?
options: A highly specific cross-tabulation, like Client Entertainment spend by region for a quarter, limited to over-policy items split by waived vs. audited
The total number of employees in the company
The company's annual revenue
The current date
questions.explain: That kind of specific, multi-dimensional cross-tabulation is exactly the ad hoc analysis OTBI is built for, versus a fixed seeded report's limited structure.

questions.q: Why does the lesson emphasize that policy design is 'a business conversation, not a technical one'?
options: Because Oracle configuration is actually impossible to complete
Because business conversations replace the need for any Oracle setup
Because the hard part is getting stakeholders to agree on defensible numbers (like a meal cap), not the technical setup once decisions are made
Because technical configuration always takes longer than stakeholder discussions
questions.explain: Once policy numbers and decisions are agreed upon, building them in Oracle is comparatively straightforward; the harder work is the business negotiation beforehand.

questions.q: What are the three numbers compared in a corporate card three-way reconciliation?
options: What the card issuer billed, what arrived in Expenses as transactions, and what has been attached to approved expense reports
The employee's salary, bonus, and tax withholding
The company's revenue, expenses, and net income
Three different currency conversion rates
questions.explain: Reconciliation compares the issuer's billed total, the transaction feed received in Expenses, and the amount actually attached to completed, approved reports.
